answer: Count the cost of replication first: one identity needs a distinct host, a funding path and a work history, so 1,000 copies need 1,000 of each before the first payout. When peer verdicts disagree, the score is diluted toward the lower verdict instead of averaged, and no identity may audit its own recruit. What breaks is the recruit chain: a farmer on the tundra cannot seed his own velvet-lined vault in one season. His copies pay, at best, half.
